newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen mixed to higher after Dow 7,000.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen mixed to higher after Dow 7,000.

text.p: Wall Street stocks are expected to open mixed to higher as investors probe uncharted territory one day after driving the Dow industrials to their first ever close above the 7,000 millennium mark.

"The futures are up slightly so I guess we'll have a mixed to higher opening," said Larry Wachtel, analyst at Prudential Securities. "I don't think people will go nuts on the upside. Are they supposed to keep buying on top of a 500-point move just because the Dow topped 7,000? I don't think so."

The market's tone will be set by a slew of economic data due ahead of the opening -- the January producer price index at 0830/1330 and January industrial production and capacity utilization at 0915/1415.

"If we get a continuation of benign inflation and if the capacity utilization number is okay we'll get a continuation of the rally. If the numbers are ugly, investors will use them as an excuse to take profits," said Phil Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line's Asset Management division.
Investors may be hesitant to make big commitments ahead of a three-day weekend, analysts said.
In Tokyo, the Nikkei average closed up 33.94 points at 18,722.
In London, the FTSE 100 Index was up 21.8 at 4348.9.

Among U.S. shares traded in London, International Business Machines Corp was up 1/4 at 146-3/8 and Intel Corp was 1/4 better at 157-1/4. Procter & Gamble Co was 1/4 firmer at 127-1/4 and Philip Morris Cos Inc gained 1/4 at 125-3/8.
The dollar hit a fresh four-year high of about 124.82 yen in Tokyo but sagged to session lows in Europe, dipping beneath 124 yen. It stayed above 168 marks.

The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street writes that people laughed at Prudential Securities chief technical analyst Ralph Acampora when he predicted Dow 7,000 back in June 1995. But it's Ralph Acampora who's laughing now, and forecasting Dow 8,250 before the year's end.

The New York Times Market Place writes that American General Corp's $1.8 billion stock pact to acquire USLIFE Corp, the largest of American General's five acquisitions over the last two years, creates a company that ranks among the four top life insurers in the country.
